clue.text: Bonus question on a location east of India

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another sits after it, so the question follows the word for a

parts.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a head' means per
QU is a standard abbreviation for question
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A quiz offers a bonus question about somewhere lying east of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' here is the 'a' of 'a pound a head', meaning for each; 'east of' in an across answer puts the location to the right of India.
explanation.definitionFit: A perquisite, or perk, is an extra benefit on top of a salary, so a bonus.

clue.text: Agreement in full announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we want a word that is said like the phrase meaning in full

parts.note: a hall that is full is packed

explanation.surface: A deal is declared publicly with every term agreed in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Vessel mirrors partly rotated without frames

indicators.note: rotated means turned round, so the portion is read from right to left
partly means only a portion of the following words is used, running across them

parts.note: the letters running across the end of vessel and the start of mirrors

explanation.surface: Mirrors on a ship, swung round, are found to lack any frames.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimless glasses or mirrors have no surrounding frame or rim.

clue.text: Not settled in lab set up within university outhouse

indicators.note: within means placed inside the outer pair of words that follow
set up here means arranged afresh, so the letters before it are reorganised

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for university
taken as written, part of the letters to rework
taken as written, completing the letters to rework
a shed is an outbuilding

explanation.surface: A research project not yet established sits in a lab built inside a college shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' looks like part of the picture of building a lab, but it reworks the letters of 'in lab set', which then sit between U and SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unestablished means not yet fixed or settled in place or position.

clue.text: Ridicule composer briefly over pay award

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Erik Satie, the French composer
a rise is an increase in pay, the British word for a raise

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a musician who has been granted a salary increase.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' puts the shortened composer above the pay award.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise is to mock or make fun of by satire, so to ridicule.

clue.text: Husband in present danger

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for present that follows

parts.note: a treat is a gift or present
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man finds himself at risk right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present danger' reads as one phrase about the here and now; 'present' is the gift word that holds the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of possible harm, so a danger.

clue.text: Drink unlimited drink

indicators.note: unlimited means without limits, so both edges of the word are removed

parts.note: pastis is an aniseed-flavoured French spirit

explanation.surface: A call for a drink with no restrictions on how much.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word serves as definition and as the source; PASTIS loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so a drink.

clue.text: Mix fish into broth that Oscar's left

indicators.note: into means put inside the broth word that follows
Oscar having left means the letter for Oscar departs from that broth word

parts.note: soup is a broth
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: stir fish into a broth that Oscar abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' looks like part of the cooking instruction, but it is the definition; the broth loses its O before taking in the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a reorganisation or mixing around of an established order.

clue.text: One terribly lean bat is always after blood?

definitions.text: One terribly lean bat is always after blood?

indicators.note: terribly means in a dreadful state, so the following letters are messed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the letters to rework

explanation.surface: A starving vampire bat forever chasing blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a very thin vampire bat is always hungry for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiable means impossible to satisfy, like an always-hungry creature that wants more.

clue.text: Cheese and so on rolled around centre of dome

indicators.note: around means wrapped about the middle letters that follow
rolled means turned over, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and so on

indicators.note: centre of picks out just the middle letters of the next word

parts.note: the middle two letters of dome

explanation.surface: Cheeses and similar foods rolled round the middle of a domed platter.
explanation.definitionFit: Comté is a hard French cheese from the Jura region.

clue.text: How one might deliver scam for renegades

parts.note: surface reading: a question about how a fraudster pulls off a con
setter's reading: split the answer 4,5 as an instruction; reversing a word for raincoats yields scam

explanation.surface: Asking how a con trick is carried out, with traitors as the culprits.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as TURN COATS: coats can be MACS, and MACS turned round gives SCAM. A mac is a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Turncoats are people who desert their side for the opposition, so renegades.

clue.text: Dismay Leo maybe turning learners into sailors

indicators.note: turning X into Y means one set of letters is swapped for another

parts.note: Leo is an example of a star group; maybe flags the example
L is learner, as on a learner driver's plate; two of them for the plural
RN is the Royal Navy, so sailors

explanation.surface: Someone born under Leo is dismayed when driving pupils become naval recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: In CONSTELLATION the LL is replaced by RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is anxiety or dismay, typically at something unexpected.

clue.text: Key shelter hosts principal cycling show?

indicators.note: hosts means takes in as a guest, so the shelter word holds the next piece
cycling means going round, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: Enter is a key on a computer keyboard
a tent is a shelter
main means principal or chief

explanation.surface: A crucial refuge welcomes a head teacher doing laps for a spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: The cycled word goes in after the first letter of the shelter, not dead centre; Enter is the keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: A show is an example of entertainment, a public performance; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Company protected by ring in novel advanced

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded by its guardian, so it goes inside

parts.note: in The Lord of the Rings Gollum calls the One Ring my precious
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm protected by a ring in a fantasy novel moves forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like the letter O, but the ring is Tolkien's, and its name in the novel is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A precocious child is advanced for its age, developing earlier than usual.

clue.text: Climber perhaps heard lines by president

indicators.note: heard means we want the sound of the next word, not its spelling

parts.note: lines are rows, said like the flower
George Bush, either of two US presidents

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is overheard reading lines written by a US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a plant that climbs, and 'perhaps' flags that a rose bush is only one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing roses are grown up walls and trellises, so a rose bush can be a climbing plant.

clue.text: Puritan regularly assumes highest state of bliss?

indicators.note: assumes means takes on or takes in, so the kept letters wrap the next word
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
top means highest

explanation.surface: A puritan routinely takes on a lofty, blissful state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' hints at a nation as well as a condition, and the question mark admits utopia is an imagined place of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect society, an ideal place or condition of happiness.

clue.text: Head counts 100 eastern Poles on applications

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
E is the abbreviation for eastern
the north and south poles, N and S
uses are applications

explanation.surface: Tallies of a hundred Poles living in the east, made through apps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it means the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of the population, literally counting heads.

clue.text: Layman Trevor is content initially on church team

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A churchgoer named Trevor is happy to play for the parish side.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so the church comes first. Celtic is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is a Scottish football club, so a team.

clue.text: Crowd outside of theatre tracks ticketed game?

parts.note: a lot is a group or crowd of people

indicators.note: outside of means the outer edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
RY stands for railway, tracks

explanation.surface: Audiences arriving outside a theatre by rail for a ticketed show.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a game of chance in which numbered tickets are drawn for prizes.

clue.text: Vengeful act on king is inspired by friend

indicators.note: to be inspired is to be breathed in, so these letters go inside the friend word

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
a pal is a friend
R is Rex, king
taken as written

explanation.surface: Revenge against a monarch is prompted by a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is inspired by' reads as cause and effect, but inspired means breathed in, so the king and 'is' go inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation against someone who has caused harm.

clue.text: Most low diamonds singer keeps with spades out at last

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the singer surrounds the diamonds

parts.note: Sade is a Nigerian-British singer
D is the card suit diamonds
S is the card suit spades

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of the word before is taken

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy card game: a singer holds diamonds while spades are finally out.
explanation.definitionFit: Low means sad or downcast, so most low is the superlative saddest.

clue.text: Rascal in the way of an African animal

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
à la means in the manner or style of

explanation.surface: A naughty child gets in the path of a beast on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the way of' reads as blocking, but 'in the way' is à la, in the style of, and 'of' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a medium-sized antelope of eastern and southern Africa.

clue.text: New Dutch tart stuffed with poultry was up to snuff

indicators.note: stuffed with means filled with, so the birds go into the middle
new means freshly made, so the letters are formed into a different order

parts.note: the letters to rework
emus are farmed birds, counted here as poultry

explanation.surface: A novel Dutch pastry stuffed with chicken proved good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The poultry is not chicken but EMUS, which are farmed for meat; their letters mix with those of 'Dutch tart'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is an idiom for being good enough, meeting the required standard.

clue.text: Runner returning somewhat enfeebled

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
somewhat means only some of the next word is used

parts.note: the letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: An athlete coming back from injury is still a bit weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; in crosswords it often means a river, something that runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elbe is a major river of central Europe, and a river runs, hence runner.

clue.text: Exaggerates image of old retired small district vicar

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the words after it are read backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a ward is an electoral district
Rev, short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: Someone inflates the reputation of a retired vicar from a small parish.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw a picture or description is to depict it in exaggerated terms.

clue.text: Best distribution of cards on second part of display

indicators.note: second part means the second letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the second letter
the deal is how cards are handed out to players

explanation.surface: The finest hand of cards dealt out for show.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' places the deal after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect or the best possible.

clue.text: Island app used to communicate when power cut

indicators.note: power cut means the letter standing for power is removed

parts.note: Skype is a video-calling app
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Islanders use an app to keep in touch during a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power cut' reads as a blackout; it means SKYPE loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Composed motets in A and E flat

indicators.note: composed means put together, as music is, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to rework, leaving out the joining word

explanation.surface: Choral pieces written in the keys of A and E flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E flat' looks like a musical key, but 'flat' is the definition, a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors, a self-contained apartment.
